result.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
result.summary: Web agents increasingly browse, shop, and manage accounts on behalf of their users. Prior work has shown that they can be misled by adversarial content, including prompt injections and deceptive interfaces. Beyond such attacks, agents operating on the open web also encounter online fraud designed to deceive humans, including fraudulent online stores, fake investment platforms, and advance-fee schemes. How web agents respond to such fraud during task execution remains underexplored, in part because scam websites are short-lived, making systematic evaluation difficult. To address this gap, we introduce ScamWorld, an interactive environment that reconstructs reported scam websites across diverse scenarios, fraud mechanisms, and languages. Each reconstructed website reproduces documented fraud mechanisms, making relevant signs of fraud observable before the agent's final action and enabling controlled, repeatable evaluation. Through an extensive study of web agents powered by six frontier LLMs, we find that baseline deception rates range from 11% to 35% across models. Agents proceed more readily with payments than with requests for credentials or wallet information. A closer analysis of agent trajectories shows that some agents acknowledge suspicious conditions yet proceed, at times treating the user's instructions as authorisation to accept additional terms imposed by the website. ScamWorld provides a reusable testbed for systematically evaluating and stress-testing web agents against real-world online fraud.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 ScamWorld 交互式环境，按已记录的诈骗机制重建多语言诈骗网站，用于可重复评测 web agent 在任务执行中是否被欺诈；六种前沿 LLM 驱动的 agent 受骗率为 11%–35%。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文发现部分 agent 已识别可疑迹象仍继续执行，这一「证据已获得却未影响最终动作」的现象，或可作为检验 LVR 中内部证据是否真正驱动决策与停止判断的评测参照，可供核查。
